coder_rounds.final_message:
I have successfully fixed the bug where `fields.Constant(None)` rejected `None` constant values during load. 

### Cause of the Bug
`Field.__init__` determines whether `None` is allowed based on `load_default` before `Constant.__init__` runs. Because `load_default` was passed via `kwargs` or set after `super().__init__(**kwargs)` in `Constant.__init__`, `allow_none` defaulted incorrectly when the constant was `None`, causing `_deserialize` or validation to raise a `ValidationError: Field may not be null.` when loading payload containing `None`.

### Solution
Updated `Constant.__init__` to prepopulate `load_default` and `allow_none` in `kwargs` before calling `super().__init__(**kwargs)`, ensuring that `allow_none` is correctly set to `True` when `constant is None`.
